ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 2, this is the situation when a motorcycle race turns a curve. At the turning place, the road surface is often higher on the outside and lower on the inside. A motorcycle has a maximum safe speed when turning. If it exceeds this speed, the motorcycle will slide. If the motorcycle slides, then which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The centripetal force provided by the resultant external force on the motorcycle is less than the required centripetal force

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 2, when a motorcycle turns on a curved road surface that is higher on the outside and lower on the inside, there is a maximum safe speed. If it exceeds this speed and slides, at this time what is the relationship between the centripetal force provided by the resultant external force on the motorcycle and the centripetal force it needs?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The centripetal force provided by the resultant external force on the motorcycle is less than the required centripetal force
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, a motorcycle and rider can be seen turning on a race track; the body of the vehicle and the rider are clearly leaning to one side, and the wheels are still in contact with the road surface, showing a state of traveling through a curve. When turning, the motorcycle undergoes curvilinear motion and needs a centripetal force directed toward the center of the circle. The question stem states that the curved road surface is “higher on the outside and lower on the inside,” and that there is a maximum safe speed for the motorcycle to turn. According to the laws of circular motion, the required centripetal force is mv^2/r; when the speed exceeds the maximum safe speed, the required centripetal force increases with v^2, exceeding the upper limit of the centripetal force that the road surface can actually provide to the motorcycle through the support force, friction force, and other actual resultant forces. Therefore, when the motorcycle slides, the centripetal force provided by the actual resultant external force is insufficient to meet the need of turning at the current speed.
